metadata.description: One grouping's recorded permission for another to use resources it holds: who granted, who received, which resources, what may be done, until when. Usually two tenants; the record is boundary-agnostic because any grouping may declare isolation. A grant permits use and never transfers ownership.

provider_ref.description: The auth-capability provider that evaluates this expression (cardinality-1 URF).

expression.description: OPAQUE provider-scoped subject expression — an LDAP DN, an OIDC claim, a K8s subject. Never parsed or evaluated by UDLM.

subject_bindings.description: External subject expressions whose holders this grouping is for: the RBAC bridge. Opaque by design; parsing or evaluating one would re-import the permission engine the model excludes.

membership_criterion.description: Which resources the grant covers, as an explicit set of uuids, `estate?uuid=in=(a,b)`. A grant names what it covers; a filter over labels or other fields would let the covered set change without anyone granting anything (#723, explicit permissions). Resources added later need the grant amended.

obligations.description: Unit-level requirements the engine enforces over the derived set, such as isolation: stores and placement partition by this grouping's uuid.

granted_by.description: The grouping that holds the resources and gives permission: a Grouping.Tenant in the common case, any isolating grouping in general. A grant across a grouping whose `obligations.isolation` is `none` permits nothing, because nothing was closed.

granted_to.description: The grouping whose members receive permission. MUST differ from `granted_by`: a grant to yourself crosses no boundary.

authorized_operations.description: What the receiving members may do: `stake` (take a share of a shareable resource), `allocate` (carve an owned portion from a pool), `read` (see declared fields). Ownership is never among them.

valid_from.description: When the grant takes effect; absent means on creation.

expires_at.description: When the grant lapses. Required. Expiry works like revocation (CTX-003): dependents go to review, nothing is seized.

threshold.description: The score the held criteria must reach for the grant to end.

kind.description: bound: the grant serves the one request, order or system in `to`. uses: at most `max` relationships under it. quota: at most `limit` of `measure` under it. time: the instant in `at`.

score.description: Weight of this criterion when it holds; negative means an exception that keeps the grant alive.

to.description: For kind bound — the request, order or system the grant serves.

max.description: For kind uses — the most relationships that may be formed under the grant.

measure.description: For kind quota — what is counted (an allocation count, or a Quantity's unit).

limit.description: For kind quota — the most of `measure` the grant allows, as a Quantity string.

ends_when.description: Criteria that end the grant before it expires (CTX-009): a threshold and scored criteria. The grant ends when the scores of the criteria that hold reach the threshold.

platform_managed.description: Set when a platform administrator created the grant on the granting grouping's behalf (CTX-004); visible to that grouping (CTX-007), and on the record rather than derived from the audit because revocation notifies the administrator as well as both groupings. Who created the grant is the audit's question, not this element's.

criteria.why: issued for one application stack; ends with it
while the stack it serves is still realized, nothing else ends the grant

context.purpose: One grouping permitting another to use something it holds. The grant is a record with its own identity and lifecycle, so it can be found, audited, time-bounded, and withdrawn.
context.plain_description: Permission for the members of one grouping to use resources held by another — who granted it, who received it, which resources, what they may do, and until when. Usually two tenants; the same record covers any pair of groupings that isolate. Withdrawing it does not seize anything: every dependent entity moves to review, and a human or policy decides whether to re-authorize, release, or migrate.
use_when: A relationship needs to cross a boundary that is otherwise closed — most often two tenants
A shared resource is used by a grouping that does not hold it
An allocation is carved from a pool another grouping holds
Members of a federation share resources while staying independent
not_for: Deciding who may act inside a tenant — external RBAC owns that (ADR-008)
Resource types that waive the per-grant requirement by standing declaration (`publicly_stakeable` / `publicly_allocatable`, CTX-008) — those need no grant at all
Ownership transfer. A grant never moves ownership; it permits use
works_with: Grouping.Tenant — the usual pair of boundaries a grant spans
The required-grant set (CTX-005) — derived from a request's edges and diffed against these
